questions.q: What is the core difference between passive and active metadata?
options: Active metadata triggers automated action downstream without a human in the triggering step; passive metadata requires a human to read and act on it
Passive metadata is more accurate than active metadata
Active metadata is always stored in a graph database, while passive metadata never is
There is no real difference — the terms describe the same thing
questions.explain: The distinction is about whether something downstream acts on the metadata automatically, not about the content of the metadata itself.

questions.q: In classification-driven masking, what role does the sensitivity tag play?
options: It actively drives real-time enforcement — a masking policy attached to the tag applies automatically on every future query
It is purely decorative and has no effect on query results
It requires a human to manually approve every single query before masking applies
It only appears in a quarterly compliance report
questions.explain: The tag isn't just a catalog label — it's the mechanism that triggers the masking policy automatically, with no human in that loop.

questions.q: What does a lineage-driven impact alert do, according to the lesson?
options: Blocks all queries against the upstream table indefinitely
Automatically notifies every owner of every downstream asset lineage shows depends on it, when an upstream asset changes
Generates a lineage diagram once per year
Deletes any downstream table automatically when an upstream table changes
questions.explain: The alert is triggered automatically by lineage data showing a dependency, without someone manually tracing the lineage diagram first.

questions.q: Why does active metadata require push-based, event-driven architecture rather than a purely pull-based one?
options: Pull-based architecture cannot technically connect to any cloud platform
Push-based architecture is always cheaper to build than pull-based architecture
A pull/crawl-based architecture only knows the current state when it's asked, on a schedule — leaving a window where a change sits unenforced
Active metadata has nothing to do with how metadata is captured
questions.explain: The lesson gives the concrete example of a sensitivity tag sitting unenforced for up to a day if the architecture only notices it on the next scheduled crawl.

questions.q: How does this lesson's active-metadata concept connect to Chapter 4, according to the lesson's own roadmap?
options: Chapter 4 repeats Chapter 3's content with no new material
Chapter 4 abandons metadata entirely and focuses only on hardware security
Active metadata has no connection to Chapter 4's topics
Chapter 4 applies the same active-metadata idea specifically to security and access — policies that read a tag and enforce access automatically
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly previews that classification-driven masking is the same mechanism Chapter 4 examines in depth as its own security architecture layer.
